concept_summary: A 3,620 sq ft bar with live entertainment and amplified sound operating until 2 a.m. at 1511 Haight Street, seeking to amend conditions of a 1996 Conditional Use Authorization for place of entertainment at this address.

overall.line: Of the 5 approvals this concept needs: 3 further review (zoning and use, entertainment permit, building permit and change of use), 1 insufficient information (alcohol licence), 1 allowed (health permit).
overall.next_step: Confirm in writing with Planning whether the 1996 CUA (Motion No. 14221) conditions allow the proposed bar use with live entertainment and amplified sound to 2 a.m., or whether a new CUA application is required to amend those conditions before filing other permits.

approvals.approval: Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit

basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)

findings.text: A Place of Entertainment permit was approved on September 8, 2016 for 609 Ashbury Street (this parcel, filed under a different address) as continuation of the 1996 CUA entertainment use (Case No. 1996.520C, Motion No. 14221).

Police Code Section 1060 et seq. requires a Place of Entertainment permit when entertainment is a primary use or shows run until 2 a.m., or a Limited Live Performance permit when live performance is secondary and ends by 10 or 11 p.m. in a performance area of 200 sq ft or less.
findings.verification_note: The record does not cite Police Code Section 1060 et seq. or mention a Limited Live Performance permit or its conditions.

findings.text: At 1566 Haight (87m away), a December 2020 CUA approved bar hours to 2 a.m. but conditioned that amplified music be limited to 10 p.m. weeknights and 2 a.m. weekends only, with soundproofing so incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises.
A Limited Live Performance permit was approved at 1569 Haight (72m away) on March 21, 2022 as an accessory use to the existing bar, taking 4 days from filing to approval.

Entertainment was denied at 1576-1580 Haight (87m away) in April 1995, and a 2008 referral confirmed the denial remained in effect with no new CUA filed, indicating the Commission views some sites as unsuitable for entertainment across multiple operators.
findings.verification_note: The records show the specific denials but do not state the general conclusion about Commission views.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: This is the original 1996 Conditional Use Authorization for this exact address (1501-1509 Haight/609 Ashbury), which approved a place of entertainment for non-amplified music in the Haight Street NCD. The concept seeks to amend this approval's conditions, making it the most directly relevant precedent.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved entertainment at this site in 1996 with non-amplified music only. Subsequent referrals in 2016-2017 (Type 48 license, Place of Entertainment permit) confirmed continuation of this use. comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved 2 a.m. bar hours but imposed strict conditions: amplified music limited to 10 p.m. weeknights and 2 a.m. weekends only, soundproofing requirements, patron behavior notices at exits, community liaison, and Entertainment Commission approval before operation. The differential hours for restaurant (10 p.m.) vs bar (2 a.m.) show the Commission can split operating conditions by…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA to amend previous authorization and add entertainment to an existing bar/restaurant at 1576-1580 Haight (87m away, same district) was denied in April 1995. This is the only denial among nearby entertainment applications and occurred at the same address that was again denied entertainment in 2008.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission denied adding entertainment to an existing bar/restaurant on this corridor in 1995. The 2008 referral (MB0800611) confirmed this denial remained in effect 13 years later, showing the Commission's entertainment denials can create long-term restrictions on specific sites even when the underlying bar/restaurant use continues.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 2008 referral documenting that the 1995 denial of Place of Entertainment at 1576-1580 Haight (87m away) remained in effect, with no new CUA filed. Same address as the 1994.633C denial, showing how denied entertainment uses are tracked over time.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning continued to deny entertainment at this site 13 years after the original 1995 denial, demonstrating that once entertainment is denied at a specific location in this district, subsequent attempts face significant precedent. The record explicitly notes no new CUA application had been filed, suggesting operators understood the denial would be difficult to overcome.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Entertainment Commission referral for Limited Live Performance permit at 1569 Haight (72m away, same NCD-HAIGHT district), approved March 2022 as accessory use to existing bar. This is an agency referral, not a use decision, but shows how entertainment can be approved when subordinate to the primary bar use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved Limited Live Performance as an accessory use to an existing bar under Section 703(d)(6), without requiring a full CUA hearing. This pathway is available for limited entertainment (200 sq ft performance area, ends by 10-11 p.m.) but would not fit a concept where live entertainment and amplified sound to 2 a.m. is a primary feature, not accessory.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation) and obtain an EIN from the IRS, then register the business with the SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector to receive a Business Account Number (BAN).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization ($70) or corporate articles ($100) with the California Secretary of State online. Within 90 days, file the Statement of Information ($20 LLC, $25 corporation). Apply for an EIN online (free, issued immediately). Then register the business in San Francisco within 30 days of starting business, paying $55–$700 based on projected gross receipts.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms a new CUA is required, file the Conditional Use Authorization application for a bar use with entertainment, including pre-application community meeting, and schedule the Planning Commission hearing (4–10 months).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File the CUA application with the Planning Department (application fee approximately $3,100–$15,000 depending on project cost). In the application, describe the bar use with live entertainment and amplified sound to 2 a.m., propose operating conditions addressing soundproofing, patron behavior, community liaison and sidewalk maintenance, and commit to Entertainment Commission approval before operation. Propose differential hours: bar to 2 a.m., amplified music to 10 p.m. weeknights and 2 a.m. weekends. Conduct the required community meeting and 300-foot mailed notice, then wait for the hearing date. Budget 120–300 days from filing to decision.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Determine whether beer and wine only or full liquor will be served. If full liquor, engage a license broker to locate and escrow an existing Type 48 license for transfer. File the ABC application with zoning sign-off from Planning.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: For beer and wine only: apply directly to ABC for a Type 42 license with the lease, seller's permit, Planning approval and 30-day posting at the premises. Expect 60–150 days if unprotested. For full liquor: hire a license broker to find an available Type 48 license (market price $100,000–$450,000 in San Francisco). Open escrow, then file the person-to-person and premises-to-premises transfer application with ABC, including the Planning CUA approval and the zoning sign-off. The transfer takes 90–240 days. In either case, ABC will refer the application to Planning and Police for review before issuing the license.

timeline_cost.notes: This range is the time to obtain the Conditional Use Authorization, Place of Entertainment permit and building permit with change of use when they are granted, based on catalog entries for those approvals. It does not include time to obtain the ABC license (which depends on whether beer and wine or full liquor is required) or the health permit (which is issued after final inspection). The CUA takes 120–300 days from filing to approval. The Place of Entertainment permit takes 45–120 days from filing to hearing and can be filed in parallel once the CUA is approved. The building permit takes 14–120 days for plan review and issuance. The cost range includes the CUA application fee ($3,100–$15,000), the POE application fee ($2,708), the building permit fee ($800–$15,000), the business registration certificate ($55–$700), the Fire Place of Assembly permit ($446), the sign permit ($300–$1,500), entity registration ($70–$150), seller's permit ($0), EDD registration ($0), RBS training ($3–$30 per person), ASCAP and BMI licenses ($600–$5,000 combined), and workers' compensation insurance (percentage of payroll, not a government fee). It does not include the ABC license cost: for beer and wine the application fee is $1,000–$1,600 and takes 60–150 days; for full liquor the market price for an existing license is $100,000–$450,000 and the transfer takes 90–240 days. The critical path is the CUA hearing (4–10 months), which must be approved before the Entertainment Commission will schedule the POE hearing. If the 1996 CUA conditions already permit this use, the CUA step drops out and the timeline shortens by 4–10 months, but that cannot be confirmed until Planning answers in writing.

records_summary: 1511 Haight Street is in the Haight Street NCD where a bar is a conditional use on the first story, and falls within the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict which requires conditional use for any new on-sale liquor establishment (Types 40, 41, 42, 47, 48, 57). The site has a long history: a Conditional Use Authorization for a place of entertainment for non-amplified music was approved in 1996 (Case No. 1996.520C), with subsequent approvals for a Place of Entertainment permit (2016) and a Type 48 license (2016, 2017) operating as Club Deluxe bar. The immediate area is saturated with alcohol uses: 21 food/drink businesses and 6 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet, triggering the undue concentration flag. Only one dated use decision has been recorded within 1,000 feet in the last 10 years—too few to establish an approval rate.
